findings.detail: Fresh lifecycle.verify_candidate(bundle, 'candidates/initial') passed. All 32 evidence items equal admitted inputs; registered source hashes, grouped marginal mappings, count fractions, retained analytic bindings and auxiliary check artifacts agree. Freeze/decision bytes were unchanged.

Static code implements the documented 40-age by 2-sex finite mixture: integer-uniform age 35-74, independent Bernoulli sex with p=2049/3547, three conditional lognormal biomarkers with explicit demographic terms and one shared Gaussian residual factor. Total rows, six columns, units and identifiers satisfy the task construction; the task supplies no exact demographic quotas.

Independent enumeration of all 80 demographic support states verifies the generator's factored demographic MGFs. Residual log variances are approximately 0.020366340000528643, 0.06942134387923761 and 0.026213875183481485, all positive. Integrating actual conditional moments recovers means 25/5.2/6.1 and total SDs 3.6/1.4/1.0, and reproduces every retained raw second moment and covariance entry.

Positive residual log variances and absolute factor loadings below one give positive-definite residual covariance. Each conditional law has positive biomarker support and finite real-power moments; a finite sum over bounded demographic states preserves those moments and all required demographic cross-products. Independent Cholesky checks confirm full population covariance rank. Mathematical support does not certify finite-precision execution.

Independent Cholesky solutions using the actual finite-mixture covariance preserve all visible adjustment sets and reproduce all slopes/intercepts. Focal E1 BMI=0.07697625734099729, E2 glucose=0.365964760039985 and E3 age=0.00443886748134946. These are assumption-dependent law consequences, not source constraints, target observations or favorable-fit criteria.
